description: Read records from one or more GitLab REST API v4 resources (projects, issues, merge requests, commits) into a DataFrame or warehouse table. Goes through GitLab's REST API with Link-header (RFC 5988) pagination and PRIVATE-TOKEN auth, supporting both GitLab.com and self-managed instances.
summary: Ingest GitLab projects, issues, merge requests, and commits.

outputs.description: One row per GitLab record (project, issue, merge request, or commit)

asset_name.label: Asset Name
asset_name.description: Name of the asset to create

access_token_env_var.label: Access Token Env Var
access_token_env_var.description: Env var with a GitLab personal, project, or group access token. Sent in the 'PRIVATE-TOKEN' header on every request (GitLab's recommended auth header -- see docs.gitlab.com/ee/api/rest/authentication.html). Required for any private project/group; a public project's read endpoints can be reached without one, but GitLab rate-limits unauthenticated requests much more aggressively.

base_url.label: Base Url
base_url.description: GitLab REST API v4 base URL. Defaults to GitLab.com SaaS. For a self-managed GitLab instance, set this to '<https://your-gitlab-host>/api/v4' -- the path must still end in '/api/v4'.

project_id.label: Project Id
project_id.description: GitLab project ID (numeric, e.g. '42') or URL-encoded path (e.g. 'my-group/my-project'). Required when `tables` includes 'issues', 'merge_requests', or 'commits' -- those are all project-scoped endpoints (GET /projects/:id/...). Not used by the 'projects' table.

group_id.label: Group Id
group_id.description: GitLab group ID (numeric) or URL-encoded path (e.g. 'my-group'). Only affects the 'projects' table: when set, lists every project in that group (GET /groups/:id/projects) instead of every project visible to the token (GET /projects, the default when neither group_id nor project_id-based scoping applies).

tables.label: Tables
tables.description: Comma-separated list of GitLab resources to query: 'projects', 'issues', 'merge_requests', 'commits'. With asset_shape='single' (default), all tables are fetched together under one asset keyed `asset_name`. With asset_shape='multi_asset', each table instead becomes its own independently-materializable Dagster asset, keyed `{asset_name}_{table}` -- materializing one table does not fetch or persist the others. 'issues'/'merge_requests'/'commits' require project_id; 'projects' uses group_id (or is unscoped) instead.

asset_shape.label: Asset Shape
asset_shape.description: 'single' (default, matches every other multi-table ingestion component in this repo, e.g. servicenow_ingestion/salesforce_ingestion/zendesk_ingestion): one asset, keyed `asset_name`, covering every table in `tables` as a single unit -- rows from every table are unioned into one returned DataFrame tagged by a `_table` column. 'multi_asset': each table in `tables` is instead its own independently-materializable asset -- select just the table(s) you want; materializing several together still batches them through one shared dlt pipeline call (one Dagster step), not parallel per-table execution. Opt into 'multi_asset' when you want to select/retry/schedule individual tables separately; stay on 'single' when you just want to monitor 'did the GitLab pipeline run'.

table_name_map.label: Table Name Map
table_name_map.description: Override the destination table name for specific GitLab resources, e.g. {'merge_requests': 'raw_mrs'}. dlt otherwise names each destination table after its GitLab resource name (the default every ingestion component in this repo relies on -- see salesforce_ingestion). Tables in `tables` that aren't listed here keep their GitLab name as-is. Every key must also appear in `tables`.

state.label: State
state.description: Filter 'issues'/'merge_requests' by state: 'opened', 'closed', 'merged' (merge_requests only), or 'locked' (merge_requests only). Unset (default) returns every state. Not used by 'projects'/'commits'.

updated_after.label: Updated After
updated_after.description: Filter 'issues'/'merge_requests' to records updated on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'). Not used by 'projects'/'commits'.

since.label: Since
since.description: Filter 'commits' to commits on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'). Only used by 'commits'.

until.label: Until
until.description: Filter 'commits' to commits on or before this ISO 8601 timestamp. Only used by 'commits'.

ref_name.label: Ref Name
ref_name.description: Branch, tag, or revision range to list 'commits' from. Defaults to the project's default branch when unset. Only used by 'commits'.

per_page.label: Per Page
per_page.description: Records fetched per API call (GitLab's 'per_page' param). Default 100, GitLab's documented maximum.

max_records.label: Max Records
max_records.description: Cap on total records returned across all pages, per table. None (default) = no cap.

verify_ssl.label: Verify Ssl
verify_ssl.description: Enable TLS verification. Set false only for self-managed instances with self-signed certs.

hash_columns.label: Hash Columns
hash_columns.description: Column names to pseudonymize (salted SHA-256, hex-encoded) before the data reaches the destination -- same deterministic-hashing pattern dlt's own docs recommend for PII (https://dlthub.com/docs/general-usage/customising-pipelines/pseudonymizing_columns). A column missing from a given resource's rows is skipped, not an error. Requires hash_salt or hash_salt_env_var.

hash_salt.label: Hash Salt
hash_salt.description: Salt for hash_columns. Required (this or hash_salt_env_var) when hash_columns is set -- a hardcoded/shared salt would let the hash be reversed by dictionary attack on common values. Use "{{ env.VAR_NAME }}" for the inline form. Keep it stable across runs: changing it changes every hash.

hash_salt_env_var.label: Hash Salt Env Var
hash_salt_env_var.description: Alternative to hash_salt: name of an env var holding the salt. Resolved at run-time.

on_schema_change.label: On Schema Change
on_schema_change.description: What to do when incoming data's shape differs from the destination table's established schema (new columns, or a column's data type changing). 'allow_all' (default, today's behavior): accept any change. 'allow_new_columns': accept new columns, but reject (fail the run) a column whose data type would change. 'block_all': reject both new columns and data type changes. A resource's own first materialization can always create its initial schema in every mode -- 'block_all' only locks down an ALREADY-established table's columns/types. A rejected change fails the run with a clear error naming the table and column -- it is never silently dropped.

exclude_columns.label: Exclude Columns
exclude_columns.description: Column names to drop from every row before it reaches the destination. Applied before hash_columns (so a column in both ends up excluded, not hashed-then-excluded). A column missing from a given resource's rows is skipped, not an error, matching hash_columns.

max_rows_per_resource.label: Max Rows Per Resource
max_rows_per_resource.description: Caps how many rows each resource loads. Unset (default): no cap. This still loads real rows into the real destination -- it is not a dry run or a preview -- meant for a first run to check a connection and the shape of the data cheaply, not for routine use. Never applied unless you set it.

destination.label: Destination
destination.description: dlt destination identifier (e.g. 'snowflake', 'bigquery', 'postgres', 'redshift', 'filesystem', 'duckdb', 'databricks', 'athena', 'clickhouse', 'mssql', 'motherduck'). Leave empty for in-memory DuckDB -> DataFrame mode.

dataset_name.label: Dataset Name
dataset_name.description: Target dataset/schema in the destination. Defaults to the asset name.

persist_only.label: Persist Only
persist_only.description: If True with destination set: emit a MaterializeResult and skip DataFrame return. If False: query the destination back into a DataFrame (only meaningful for SQL destinations -- non-SQL destinations always emit MaterializeResult).

destination_credentials_url.label: Destination Credentials Url
destination_credentials_url.description: Inline connection string passed to dlt's destination factory. Useful when one Dagster project ingests into multiple accounts of the same destination type. If unset, dlt resolves credentials from env vars -- see ../DESTINATIONS.md.

destination_credentials_env_var.label: Destination Credentials Env Var
destination_credentials_env_var.description: Alternative to destination_credentials_url: name of an env var holding the connection string. Resolved at run-time.

bucket_url.label: Bucket Url
bucket_url.description: Bucket/path URL for filesystem-shaped storage (e.g. 's3://my-bucket/path', 'gs://my-bucket/path', 'az://my-container/path', or 'file:///local/path'). Required when destination='filesystem' (the final write target). Also used as the staging area when destination='databricks' or 'athena', both of which require an intermediate filesystem stage before the warehouse-side load -- dlt resolves the bucket's credentials from the destination-appropriate standard environment variables (e.g. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) unless destination_credentials_url/destination_credentials_env_var is set.

athena_query_result_bucket.label: Athena Query Result Bucket
athena_query_result_bucket.description: Optional S3 path where Athena writes query results (e.g. 's3://my-bucket/results/'). Only used when destination='athena'. May be omitted to use Athena-managed query results instead.

deps.description: Lineage-only upstream asset keys (no data passed at runtime).
deps.label: Deps

partition_type.description: Enable partitioning: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly', 'hourly' for time-based; 'static' for a fixed set of values (e.g. customers); 'multi' for date × static (e.g. day × customer). Leave empty for unpartitioned.
partition_type.label: Partition Type

partition_cron_schedule.label: Partition Cron Schedule
partition_cron_schedule.description: Required when partition_type='cron'. A cron expression restricting the date axis to a custom cadence, e.g. '0 0 * * 1-5' for weekdays only (business-day cadence). Built on Dagster's TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition(cron_schedule=...).

partition_cron_fmt.label: Partition Cron Fmt
partition_cron_fmt.description: strftime format for partition keys produced by partition_type='cron'. Only change this for a sub-daily cron_schedule.

partition_end_offset.label: Partition End Offset
partition_end_offset.description: Passed through to the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition. 0 (the Dagster default) means a time-based partition set only ever holds COMPLETED windows -- e.g. a daily set never includes today until tomorrow. Set to 1 to include the current, still-in-progress window.

partition_timezone.label: Partition Timezone
partition_timezone.description: IANA timezone for the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition (defaults to UTC when unset, matching Dagster's own default).

partition_start.description: ISO date string for the first partition, e.g. '2024-01-01'. Required for time-based and multi partition types.
partition_start.label: Partition Start Date

partition_date_column.label: Partition Date Column
partition_date_column.description: Column used to filter the returned DataFrame to the current date partition key.

partition_dimensions.description: Multi-axis partition spec: list of {name, type, start, values, dynamic_partition_name} dicts. Overrides flat fields when set.
partition_dimensions.label: Partition Dimensions

partition_values.description: Comma-separated values for static or multi partitioning, e.g. 'acme_corp,globex,initech'. Required for static and multi types.
partition_values.label: Partition Values

partition_static_dim.label: Partition Static Dim
partition_static_dim.description: Dimension name for the static axis in multi-partitioning, e.g. 'customer' or 'region'.

partition_static_column.label: Partition Static Column
partition_static_column.description: Column used to filter the returned DataFrame to the current static/dynamic partition key (e.g. 'customer_id').

backfill_policy.label: Backfill Policy
backfill_policy.description: Backfill strategy for a partitioned asset. 'single_run' materializes a whole backfill range in one run (rows are filtered to the whole range); 'multi_run' launches one run per partition, optionally capped by backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run. Unset keeps Dagster's default. Needs a partition-range-aware IO manager for single_run.

backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.label: Backfill Policy Max Partitions Per Run
backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.description: For backfill_policy='multi_run' only: maximum partitions materialized per run (default 1).

owners.description: Asset owners — team names (team:analytics) or email addresses.
owners.label: Owners

asset_tags.description: Key-value tags applied to the asset in the Dagster catalog, e.g. {"domain": "finance"}.
asset_tags.label: Asset Tags

kinds.description: Asset kinds shown in the Dagster catalog (e.g. snowflake, python). Auto-inferred from component name if empty.
kinds.label: Kinds

freshness_max_lag_minutes.description: Maximum acceptable lag in minutes before this asset is considered stale.
freshness_max_lag_minutes.label: Freshness Max Lag (minutes)

freshness_cron.description: Cron schedule for the freshness policy, e.g. '0 9 * * 1-5' (weekdays 9am).
freshness_cron.label: Freshness Cron Schedule

include_preview_metadata.label: Include Preview Metadata
include_preview_metadata.description: Include a preview of the output data in metadata (first 5 rows as a markdown table). Used by builder UIs to render asset shape without warehouse access.

preview_rows.label: Preview Rows
preview_rows.description: Rows to include in the preview metadata when `include_preview_metadata` is True. For long DataFrames (>10x preview_rows), a random sample is used so the preview reflects the data distribution; otherwise head() is used.

retry_policy_max_retries.description: Max retries on asset failure. Defines a RetryPolicy. Useful for transient network failures, rate limits, etc.
retry_policy_max_retries.label: Retry Policy Max Retries

description.label: Description
description.description: Asset description shown in the Dagster catalog.

name: GitLab Ingestion
